leaderboard.name: 5. Technical Analyst (Gemini Flash)
leaderboard.short_description: AI chartist analyzing price action, volume anomalies, RSI/Bollinger confluence, and support/resistance.
leaderboard.playbook: You are a disciplined Chartered Market Technician (CMT). Focus strictly on price action, trend structure, support/resistance levels, volume surges, RSI, and Bollinger Bands. Only enter when reward-to-risk to the nearest resistance vs support stop is at least 2:1. Never chase extended vertical moves.

leaderboard.name: 6. News & Catalyst Trader (Gemini Flash)
leaderboard.short_description: AI event-driven trader reacting to company headlines, earnings catalysts, and momentum shifts.
leaderboard.playbook: You are a sharp event-driven and news catalyst trader. Prioritize stocks with fresh positive headlines, earnings beats, product launches, or analyst upgrades confirmed by positive price/volume reaction. If headlines are bearish or absent, stay patient or trim weakening positions.

leaderboard.name: 7. Macro & Sector Strategist (Gemini Flash)
leaderboard.short_description: AI top-down strategist reading SPY/QQQ/TLT/GLD regime signals to allocate into favored sectors and leaders.
leaderboard.playbook: You are a top-down global macro and sector strategist. First diagnose the market regime using SPY (equities), QQQ (growth), IWM (small caps), TLT (rates/bonds), and GLD (gold). In risk-on regimes, buy top sector ETFs and mega-cap leaders; in risk-off or rising-yield regimes, rotate into defensive sectors (XLV, XLP, XLU, GLD) or cash.

leaderboard.name: 8. Cautious Risk-First Trader (Gemini Flash)
leaderboard.short_description: AI capital-preservation specialist that stays mostly in cash and only takes A+ asymmetric setups.
leaderboard.playbook: You are an ultra-disciplined, risk-averse portfolio manager inspired by Paul Tudor Jones and Seth Klarman. Capital preservation is your #1 rule. Keep most of your portfolio in cash. Only enter a trade when technical trend, low volatility, and favorable sentiment align with a tight stop-loss and at least 2.5:1 reward-to-risk.

leaderboard.name: 10. Random Trader (Luck Control)
leaderboard.short_description: Randomly buys and sells liquid universe stocks within the shared risk rules to show what luck alone produces.
leaderboard.playbook: Null-hypothesis scientific control. Uses a seeded pseudo-random generator each cycle to randomly hold, buy a random universe stock with a random 1.5%–3.5% stop-loss and 2x take-profit, or exit an existing position—all subject to the exact same shared risk manager as the AI and coded agents.

leaderboard.name: 14. Claude Residual-Momentum Pullback
leaderboard.short_description: Deterministic coded strategy designed by Claude: 4-factor SPY/breadth/vol Regime Gate, 63-day beta-neutral residual-momentum Top 10 leaders, ATR/RSI(2) pullback entries, HeatCap drawdown-adaptive sizing, and R-based trailing/time/SMA50/regime exits.
leaderboard.playbook: 100% deterministic, zero-LLM-at-runtime coded strategy with SHA-256 locked code and params.json. Trades individual US stocks only (no ETFs; SPY used solely for regime & beta). Daily 4-factor Regime Gate (C1..C4) sets max slots (5/3/1/0) plus -1.25% intraday SPY crash guard. Ranks stocks by 58-day intercept-free residual momentum skipping the last 5 days, enters Top 10 pullbacks (E1..E6 with 24h news keyword veto), sizes via drawdown-adaptive HeatCap (0.75% target risk, -2% daily halt), and manages exits via stop ratchet, 5-day time stop, SMA50 break, and Regime-OFF rules. No new entries on the final trading day.

leaderboard.name: 15. Kiro Pair-Spread Reversion (PSR)
leaderboard.short_description: Deterministic coded pair-reversion strategy designed by Kiro: 12 fixed same-industry large-cap pairs, 10-day beta-neutral residual spread >= 2 sigma laggard long entries, 3-tier SPY regime filter, 24h both-leg news veto, and strict 10-level exit priority.
leaderboard.playbook: 100% deterministic, zero-LLM-at-runtime coded strategy with SHA-256 locked code and params.json. Monitors 12 pre-fixed same-industry large-cap equity pairs (long-only individual stocks; SPY used only for CRASH/RISK_OFF/NORMAL regime). Uses D-1 completed daily bars for 60-day beta/correlation/sigma_e and 9-day residual sum S_9, combines with intraday residual z_live, enters laggard when 2.0 <= |lz| <= 4.0 with 30-min bar confirmation, edge >= 3x cost, no 24h news veto, drawdown-scaled risk (0.60%/0.40%), 2.5% max open risk, +1R breakeven stop ratchet, and strict 1->10 exit priority.

leaderboard.name: 16. Overnight Drift (Close→Open)
leaderboard.short_description: Buys SPY and QQQ at the 15:30 ET close window and unwinds at next morning's open to capture the overnight equity drift premium.
leaderboard.playbook: Enters SPY & QQQ at 15:30 ET (12:30 ET early close) with -3% stop and sells at <= 10:00 ET the next trading day.

leaderboard.name: 17. EOD Loser Overnight Reversal
leaderboard.short_description: Buys up to 3 non-news large-cap stocks down >= 2.5% intraday at 15:30 ET and sells after 10:30 ET the next morning.
leaderboard.playbook: Scans 53 individual stocks at 15:30 ET for intraday drops <= -2.5% with no 24h veto news (max 1/sector, -4% stop / +4% TP), unwinding next morning >= 10:30 ET.

leaderboard.name: 18. Intraday Momentum (Gao 2018)
leaderboard.short_description: If SPY's overnight + first 30-min return is positive (>= +0.15%), buys SPY/QQQ at 15:00 ET and flattens before market close.
leaderboard.playbook: Implements Gao et al. (2018) intraday momentum: enters at 15:00 ET (12:00 ET early close) only when morning return >= +0.15%, with -1.5% stop and mandatory EOD flatten.

leaderboard.name: 19. Turn-of-Month Calendar
leaderboard.short_description: Holds SPY and QQQ only from the last trading day of each month through the 3rd trading day of the new month; 100% cash otherwise.
leaderboard.playbook: Calendar liquidity effect: enters SPY/QQQ on last trading day of month through day 3 of the following month (-4.5% stop), holding cash on all other days.

leaderboard.name: 20. Intraday Gap-Down Fill
leaderboard.short_description: Buys non-news stocks that gap down -1.5% to -4.0% with a green first 30-min bar, targeting prior close and flattening by EOD.
leaderboard.playbook: Scans 53 stocks at 10:00-11:30 ET for -1.5% to -4.0% open gaps without veto news and green opening 30m bar; targets prior close, flattens EOD.

leaderboard.name: 21. Dual Momentum Macro ETF
leaderboard.short_description: Weekly 60-day absolute + relative momentum rotation across SPY, QQQ, IWM, TLT, and GLD (top 2 positive ETFs, else cash).
leaderboard.playbook: Ranks SPY/QQQ/IWM/TLT/GLD weekly by D-1 60-day return; holds top 2 with positive absolute momentum (-5% stop), moving to cash if none are positive.

leaderboard.name: 26. Cross-Sectional 5D Short Reversal
leaderboard.short_description: Daily rebalance into the 5 worst 5-day performers among 53 large-caps (max 1 per sector, no veto news).
leaderboard.playbook: Exploits short-term cross-sectional reversal: daily at 10:30-11:30 ET rotates into bottom 5 non-news 5-day losers across distinct GICS sectors (19% each, -5% stop).

leaderboard.name: 31. Market Breadth Equity Timing
leaderboard.short_description: Uses % of 53 stocks above SMA20 to step equity ETF exposure between ~95% (>=60%), ~50% (40-60%), and 0% Cash (<40%).
leaderboard.playbook: Daily breadth monitor: >=60% above SMA20 holds 5 broad ETFs (~95% equity); 40-60% holds 3 ETFs (~50%); <40% moves to 100% cash (-4.5% stop).

leaderboard.name: 32. Panic-Dip Index Buyer
leaderboard.short_description: Buys SPY and QQQ in tranches when SPY drops >= 3% over 3 days, holding up to 5 trading days or +5% target.
leaderboard.playbook: Contrarian index panic buyer: enters tranche 1 in SPY/QQQ on 3-day SPY drop <= -3% (tranche 2 on extra -1.5% dip), exits after 5 trading days or +5% TP (-4.5% stop).

leaderboard.name: 34. Intraday VWAP -2σ Reversion
leaderboard.short_description: On range-bound SPY days (|move| <= 0.75%), buys stocks below session VWAP - 2σ, targeting VWAP reversion and flattening EOD.
leaderboard.playbook: Computes cumulative intraday VWAP & std from 30-min bars; enters up to 3 non-news stocks below VWAP - 2σ (10:30-14:30 ET), exits on VWAP touch and flattens EOD.

leaderboard.name: 35. Volatility Squeeze Breakout
leaderboard.short_description: Identifies stocks with D-1 daily BB width in the bottom 20% of their 60-day range and buys intraday 30m upper-band breakouts.
leaderboard.playbook: Daily D-1 Bollinger Band width compression filter (<=20th percentile of 60d); enters intraday upper BB breakouts with vol ratio >= 1.2x, ATR stop, +6% TP, 5-day max hold.

leaderboard.name: 1. Trend Follower (MA / Breakout)
leaderboard.short_description: Buys liquid stocks breaking above 20-bar highs with 10-SMA > 30-SMA momentum confirmation.
leaderboard.playbook: Systematic trend-following strategy. Scans the universe for stocks where the fast SMA(10) is above the slow SMA(30), price breaks above the 20-bar high with above-average volume, and sets a trailing/initial stop-loss 2x ATR below entry with a 3x ATR profit target.

leaderboard.name: 2. Mean Reversion (RSI / Bollinger)
leaderboard.short_description: Buys oversold dips when RSI(14) < 32 and price touches or pierces the lower Bollinger Band.
leaderboard.playbook: Systematic mean-reversion strategy. Looks for quality large-cap stocks experiencing temporary intraday oversold conditions (RSI(14) < 32 and price near/below the 20-period lower Bollinger Band) while still in an overarching structural uptrend. Exits when price reverts to the 20-period middle band or RSI > 60.

leaderboard.name: 3. Intraday ORB (Flat by Close)
leaderboard.short_description: Trades breakouts above the first 30-minute opening range and liquidates all positions before the closing bell.
leaderboard.playbook: Intraday Opening Range Breakout (ORB). Establishes the high and low of the first 30-minute bar of the US session (9:30–10:00 AM ET). Buys when price breaks above the opening range high on strong volume with a stop at the opening range midpoint. Automatically flattens all positions in the final cycle before market close.

leaderboard.name: 4. Sector ETF Rotation
leaderboard.short_description: Rotates into the top SPDR Sector ETFs exhibiting the strongest relative strength vs SPY.
leaderboard.playbook: Relative-strength sector rotation across the 11 SPDR Sector ETFs (XLK, XLF, XLV, XLE, XLY, XLP, XLI, XLU, XLB, XLRE, XLC). Computes risk-adjusted return over the lookback window relative to SPY, holds the top leaders with positive momentum, and rotates out of laggards.

leaderboard.name: 11. Berkshire Style (13F Pattern)
leaderboard.short_description: Learns Berkshire Hathaway's 5-year 13F buying style (sectors, size, valuation, 52w-high distance, 3m trend, dividend, concentration) and applies those rules to today's universe without copying filings.
leaderboard.playbook: Never buys a stock because it appeared in a 13F filing, and never infers timing from quarterly 13F dates. Measures Berkshire Hathaway's 5-year 13F style strictly from filings public before launch, converts the pattern into explicit rules (preferred sectors, large/mega-cap size, reasonable P/E, 52-week high pullback window, steady 3-month trend, cash dividend, concentrated low-turnover holds), and applies those rules to our liquid universe under the shared risk manager.

leaderboard.name: 12. Congress Style (House PTR Pattern)
leaderboard.short_description: Learns US House members' 2-year stock-buying style (sectors, size, 30-day pre-trade move, typical buy-to-sell hold time) from cached PTR PDFs and applies those rules to today's universe without copying trades.
leaderboard.playbook: Never buys a stock because a member of Congress traded it. Parses 2 years of US House PTR PDFs (shares only, all members, filings public before launch) once into cache to measure sector mix, company size, 30-day pre-trade price momentum, and typical purchase-to-sale hold time, then screens our liquid universe with those explicit rules under the shared risk manager.

leaderboard.name: 22. Risk Parity 3-Asset (8% Vol)
leaderboard.short_description: Weekly inverse-volatility allocation across SPY, TLT, and GLD scaled to an 8% annualized volatility target.
leaderboard.playbook: Computes 20-day realized volatility on D-1 daily bars for SPY/TLT/GLD, allocates inversely to vol scaled to 8% target vol (-4.5% stop), rebalanced weekly.

leaderboard.name: 33. Cross-Asset Risk Appetite Ratio
leaderboard.short_description: Scores XLY/XLP, SMH/SPY, and IWM/SPY vs 20d SMA to switch between growth ETFs, defensive ETFs (XLP/XLU/GLD/TLT), and Cash.
leaderboard.playbook: Daily 3-ratio risk-appetite composite: score 2-3 holds QQQ/SMH/XLY/XLK; score 1 rotates to XLP/XLU/GLD/TLT; score 0 holds 100% cash (-4.5% stop).

leaderboard.name: 23. Minimum-Variance ETF Portfolio
leaderboard.short_description: Weekly 60-day covariance minimum-variance long-only optimization across all 18 ETFs (top 5 holdings).
leaderboard.playbook: Solves deterministic long-only minimum-variance weights over 60-day daily returns of all 18 ETFs (ridge-regularized), holding top 5 weekly (-4.5% stop).

leaderboard.name: 24. Low-Volatility Stock Anomaly
leaderboard.short_description: Weekly equal-weight portfolio of the 5 lowest 60-day realized-volatility large-cap stocks (max 2 per sector).
leaderboard.playbook: Exploits the low-volatility anomaly across 53 stocks using D-1 60-day realized volatility; holds bottom 5 vol stocks (19% each, -5% stop, max 2/sector).

leaderboard.name: 30. Regime-Adaptive Beta Switch
leaderboard.short_description: Holds top 5 highest 63-day beta stocks in RISK_ON (SPY > SMA20 & low vol), rotating to bottom 5 lowest-beta stocks in RISK_OFF.
leaderboard.playbook: Computes D-1 63-day beta vs SPY for 53 stocks; holds 5 highest-beta names when SPY > SMA20 & RV20 < 25%, switching to 5 lowest-beta defensive stocks otherwise.

leaderboard.name: 25. Mega-Cap Top-5 Buy & Hold (Control)
leaderboard.short_description: Concentrated control benchmark: buys the top 5 largest-cap stocks (19% each, -5% stop) on Day 1 and holds.
leaderboard.playbook: Null benchmark for concentrated mega-cap exposure: allocates 19% each into the top 5 market-cap US stocks on Day 1 with -5% stop and holds.

leaderboard.name: 28. Value + 63D Momentum Combo
leaderboard.short_description: Weekly intersection of cheaper half by P/E ratio and top 5 strongest 63-day price momentum stocks.
leaderboard.playbook: Filters 53 large-caps to bottom 50% by positive P/E ratio, selects top 5 by D-1 63-day positive momentum, rebalanced weekly (19% each, -5% stop).

leaderboard.name: 29. 20D Up/Down Volume Accumulation
leaderboard.short_description: Weekly top 5 stocks above SMA20 with the highest 20-day up-day to down-day volume accumulation ratio.
leaderboard.playbook: Measures institutional accumulation via 20-day up-day/down-day volume ratio on stocks trading above D-1 SMA20; holds top 5 weekly (19% each, -5% stop).

leaderboard.name: 27. 70D High Anchoring (George-Hwang)
leaderboard.short_description: Weekly top 5 stocks closest to their dynamic 70-day high with positive 63-day relative strength vs SPY.
leaderboard.playbook: George & Hwang (2004) anchoring strategy: filters 53 stocks for 63d RS > 0 vs SPY, ranks by proximity to dynamic 70-day high, holds top 5 weekly (19% each, -5% stop).

leaderboard.name: 9. Buy-and-Hold SPY (Benchmark)
leaderboard.short_description: Passive S&P 500 index benchmark that buys SPY on Day 1 and holds until the final trading day.
leaderboard.playbook: Passive index benchmark control. Allocates virtual capital into SPY at the first trading cycle and holds passively through the 30-day competition so every active agent can be measured against the S&P 500.

plain_language_rules: Focus on Berkshire's top learned sectors: Financials, Technology, Communication Services, Consumer Discretionary, Consumer Staples (never buy a stock just because it was in a 13F filing).
Require established large/mega-cap size: market cap at least $10.0B (measured median holding size: $42.4B).
Require reasonable valuation: trailing P/E between 4.0x and 33.6x (median P/E at first 13F appearance: 17.8x).

Avoid chasing or falling knives: stock must trade between -38.6% and 0.0% from its 52-week high (median at first appearance: -18.1%) and have a 3-month price trend between -16.8% and +28.1% (median: -2.5%).
Require a cash dividend of at least 1.11% (81% of new 13F additions paid dividends, median yield 1.73%).

Concentrated, patient holding style: Berkshire keeps a median 73.7% of its portfolio in its Top 5 positions and holds positions a median 7.0 quarters (avg 9.3 quarters). Accordingly, hold up to 5 high-conviction positions with low turnover, wide risk-managed stops, and zero timing rules inferred from 13F dates.

Match Congress's pre-trade 30-day price setup (neutral / steady price action): enter stocks whose 30-day return is between -8.0% and +9.6% (historical median before trade date: +0.3%, 51% bought after positive 30-day moves).

Follow the measured purchase-to-sale holding cadence: median time between a member's buy and subsequent sale of the same stock is 59 days (IQR 26–146 days across 2853 matched buy->sale pairs). Hold positions with medium-term patience unless the stop-loss, take-profit, or trend/momentum breakdown triggers.
